newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New Asia markets face tough controls - Jardine.
newsitem.headline: New Asia markets face tough controls - Jardine.

text.p: In the aftermath of the Barings trading disaster, there is less risk that new futures markets in Asia will start out under-regulated, William Grossman, a director of Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said on Thursday.
But some markets in the fast-growing Asian setting for new exchanges are being established under overly-strict regulatory controls, Grossman said in an interview.

"Korea has excellent potential from the perspective of market users but the regulations are so protective that a lot of business is being driven away," he said. To a lesser extent, the same thing is happening in Malaysia, Grosmman said.
But Grossman said that given the Barings debacle, over-regulation "is probably the lesser of two evils."

The possibility of a similar Barings-type incident occurring on another exchange is causing some to err on the side of over-protection, he said. Former Barings trader Nick Leeson was able to run up around US$1.25 billion in derivatives trading losses using the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) and Osaka exchange, breaking the British mnerchant bank in 1995.
Grossman was attending the Asia-Pacific Futures Forum in Sydney, where delegates on Wednesday called for an intermarket surveillance group to monitor activity on exchanges in the Asia-Pacifc region.
